must_remember: Absolute refractive index $n$ is defined as $n = c/v$ and is always $\ge 1$ for material media.
Relative refractive index $n_{21} = n_2 / n_1 = v_1 / v_2$.
Total Internal Reflection occurs only from denser ($n_1$) to rarer ($n_2$) medium when angle of incidence exceeds critical angle $\theta_c = \sin^{-1}(n_2/n_1)$.
Frequency of light remains constant across medium boundaries, while speed and wavelength change.
Group refractive index accounts for wave packets: $n_g = n - \lambda \left(\frac{dn}{d\lambda}\right)$.
Electromagnetic relation: $n = \sqrt{\mu_r \varepsilon_r}$, with $\mu_r \approx 1$ for non-magnetic media giving $n \approx \sqrt{\varepsilon_r}$.

glossary.meaning: The ratio of the speed of light in vacuum to the speed of light in a given medium.
The ratio of the refractive index of medium 2 to that of medium 1, representing the ratio of wave speeds $v_1 / v_2$.
The angle of incidence in the denser medium for which the angle of refraction in the rarer medium is $90^\circ$.
Empirical material-dependent constants used in Cauchy's dispersion relation to describe wavelength dependence of refractive index.
Refractive index relevant to the propagation velocity of a wave packet or pulse in a dispersive medium.
